pages.note: THE CHANT ENDS ON THIS SHEET. Twenty-one TWO-COLUMN rows (gutter measured at 216px, x 920-1135, over the two-column block ALONE), then a centred bold colophon, then a rule and a footnote at the foot. Subrahmā and Sanaṅkumāra come, Māra's army advances and is dispersed, and the Buddha names the disciples who have won the battle.

closing.pali: มะหาสะมะยะสุตตัง นิฏฐิตัง.
closing.english: Here ends the Discourse on the Great Gathering.

working_notes.invitation: None printed; this is the end of the chant.
working_notes.units: Twenty-one, all of them two-column rows. The colophon and the footnote are NOT verses: the first is the chant's `closing`, the second its `source_printed` — the same division page 158 used when the Mahāsatipaṭṭhāna ended.
working_notes.ordering: Pali only. No Thai translation is printed anywhere on this sheet.
working_notes.conventions: The whole-page gutter profile FAILED on this sheet and was re-run over the two-column block alone. Every closing mark and every cluster mark was read from magnified crops.
working_notes.pages: IMG_0453.PNG, page 182, the number printed clearly at the top centre. Completes the chant begun on 175. A hand grips the left edge, outside the text block.

checks.issue: ⚠ THE WHOLE-PAGE GUTTER PROFILE FINDS NO CORRIDOR ON THIS SHEET, and the page is nevertheless in two columns. The centred bold colophon at the foot spans the gutter — its ink runs x 816-1322, straight across the corridor — so a profile taken over the full height reports a single column and would have merged the two columns into one reading. Re-profiled over the TWO-COLUMN BLOCK ALONE (y 240-2125) the gutter appears plainly: 216px at x 920-1135. This is the same failure that page 170 produced, where a centred title closed the corridor. Profile per BLOCK, never per page.

THE CHANT ENDS HERE and its ‼ CONTINUES marker comes off. The centred bold line มะหาสะมะยะสุตตัง นิฏฐิตัง. is the chant's `closing`, not a verse and not a page block; the footnote under the rule is a CANONICAL CITATION and goes in `source_printed`. That is the division page 158 used for the identical arrangement at the end of the Mahāsatipaṭṭhāna, and it is followed here.

NOTHING ELSE ON THIS SHEET. Walked top to bottom against the photograph: the page number 182 at the top centre, twenty-one two-column rows, the centred colophon, the rule, the footnote. No title, no invitation, no section heading, no section_end label and no rubric. An ink-profile of the full width returns exactly 24 bands — the page number, twenty-one rows with one pair merged, the colophon, the rule and the footnote line — and nothing unaccounted for.

⚠ สันนังกุมาโร IS PRINTED WITH DOUBLE น, giving `sannaṅkumāro`, where the roman twin verse 173 sets `Sanaṅkumāro` with a single n. He is Sanaṅkumāra, the Ever-Young Brahmā, and the canon has the single n. Read at 2.6×; the two น are plainly separate letters. Entered as this page prints it.

⚠ อุปปันโน IS PRINTED WITH DOUBLE ป, giving `uppanno`, where the roman twin verse 175 sets `Upapanno` and the canon has upapanno, 'reborn'. Read at 2.6×. The two readings are different words, not a spelling variant — uppanna is 'arisen' and upapanna is 'reborn' — so this is worth putting to the book rather than settling from the twin. Entered as this page prints it.

MĀRA'S COMMAND IS UNPUNCTUATED AND UNMARKED ON THIS SHEET. The roman twin sets it as separate sentences inside quotation marks — `’Etha. Gaṇhatha. Bandhatha. Rāgena bandhamatthu vo.` at 180 and `Samantā parivāretha. Mā vo muñcittha koci naṃ.’` at 181 — where this page prints เอถะ คัณหะถะ พันธะถะ and สะมันตา ปะริวาเรถะ with no internal stops and no quotes at all. Entered as printed, at both verses 155 and 156; the English keeps the sense of a shouted order.

A PUNCTUATION DIFFERENCE FROM THE TWIN. This sheet closes the line with a FULL STOP after จักขุมา, where the roman copy's verse 186 has no mark and runs straight on into 187. Entered as this page prints it.

THE BUDDHA'S ADDRESS IS UNMARKED ON THIS SHEET. The roman twin ends its verse 187 with a COLON and wraps 188 in quotation marks, making `Mārasenā abhikkantā. Te vijānātha bhikkhavo` the Buddha's own words; and it does the same again at 191-192 for the closing verse. This page prints all of them plain. Entered as printed; the English keeps the sense of direct speech.

A WORD-DIVISION DIFFERENCE FROM THE TWIN on the chant's last line, letters identical. This sheet sets ชะเนสุตาติ as one word, giving `janesutāti`; the roman copy's verse 192 sets `jane sutā`ti` as two with a closing quotation mark. Entered as this page prints it. The superscript ¹ keying the footnote sits immediately after this word's full stop.

THE COLOPHON CARRIES A FULL STOP, where page 158's did not — that sheet printed มะหาสะติปัฏฐานะสุตตะปาโฐ นิฏฐิโต bare. Both are entered as their own sheet prints them. ⚠ NOTE ALSO that the agreement here is CORRECT: สุตตัง is neuter and takes นิฏฐิตัง, which is what this sheet gives. That is worth recording because page 110 got the same agreement wrong, printing a feminine นิฏฐิตา against a neuter สุตตัง.

THE CLUSTER MARK IS THANTHAKHAT ์ THROUGHOUT, and this sheet carries more of them than any other in the chant — สุพ์รัห์มา and สะหัสสะพ์รัห์มะโลกานัง and มะหาพ์รัห์มาภิติฏฐะติ and สะพ์รัห์มะเก each take TWO, on พ and on ห; then ภิส์มากาโย, กัต์วานะ, วะวักขิต์วานะ and สุต์วา take one each. All read from magnified crops. Consistent with the rest of the chant, which never uses yamakkan ๎.

A WORD-DIVISION DIFFERENCE FROM THE TWIN, letters identical. This sheet sets ตะละมาหัจจะ as one word, giving `talamāhacca`; the roman copy's verse 183 hyphenates it `tala-māhacca`. The twin hyphenates several compounds this sheet runs together; recorded once here for the group.

verses.pali: สุพ์รัห์มา ปะระมัตโต จะ ปุตตา อิทธิมะโต สะหะ
verses.pali_roman: Subrahmā paramatto ca puttā iddhimato saha
verses.english: Subrahmā and Paramatta, and the sons of the Mighty One with them,

verses.pali: สันนังกุมาโร ติสโส จะ โสปาคะ สะมิติง วะนัง.
verses.pali_roman: Sannaṅkumāro tisso ca sopāga samitiṃ vanaṃ.
verses.english: Sanaṅkumāra and Tissa — he too came to the wood, to the assembly.

verses.pali: สะหัสสะพ์รัห์มะโลกานัง มะหาพ์รัห์มาภิติฏฐะติ
verses.english: Over a thousand Brahmā-worlds the Great Brahmā presides,

verses.pali: อุปปันโน ชุติมันโต ภิส์มากาโย ยะสัสสิ โส.
verses.english: arisen there, radiant, awesome of form, and glorious.

verses.pali: ทะเสตถะ อิสสะรา อาคู ปัจเจกะวะสะวัตติโน
verses.english: Ten lords came here, each wielding his own power,

verses.pali: เตสัญจะ มัชฌะโต อาคา หาริโต ปะริวาริโต.
verses.english: and in the midst of them came Hārita with his retinue about him.

verses.pali: เต จะ สัพเพ อะภิกกันเต สินเท เทเว สะพ์รัห์มะเก
verses.pali_roman: Te ca sabbe abhikkante sinde deve sabrahmake
verses.english: And when all these had come, the devas with Inda and with Brahmā,

verses.pali: มาระเสนา อะภิกกามิ ปัสสะ กัณหัสสะ มันทิยัง.
verses.english: Māra's army came on — see the folly of the Dark One!

verses.pali: เอถะ คัณหะถะ พันธะถะ ราเคนะ พันธะมัตถุ โว
verses.pali_roman: Etha gaṇhatha bandhatha rāgena bandhamatthu vo
verses.english: Come, seize them, bind them — let them be bound to you by lust!

verses.pali: สะมันตา ปะริวาเรถะ มา โว มุญจิตถะ โกจิ นัง.
verses.pali_roman: Samantā parivāretha mā vo muñcittha koci naṃ.
verses.english: Surround them on every side — let not one of them escape you!

verses.pali: อิติ ตัตถะ มะหาเสโน กัณหะเสนัง อะเปสะยิ
verses.english: So there the great commander sent forth his dark army,

verses.pali: ปาณินา ตะละมาหัจจะ สะรัง กัต์วานะ เภระวัง.
verses.english: striking the ground with his hand and making a terrible sound —

verses.pali: ยะถา ปาวุสสะโก เมโฆ ถะนะยันโต สะวิชชุโก
verses.english: as a storm-cloud of the rains thunders with its lightning.

verses.pali: ตะทา โส ปัจจุทาวัตติ สังกุทโธ อะสะยังวะเส.
verses.english: Then he drew back, enraged and not master of himself.

verses.pali: ตัญจะ สัพพัง อะภิญญายะ วะวักขิต์วานะ จักขุมา.
verses.english: And knowing all that, the One with Vision considered it,

verses.pali: ตะโต อามันตะยิ สัตถา สาวะเก สาสะเน ระเต
verses.pali_roman: Tato āmantayi satthā sāvake sāsane rate
verses.english: and then the Teacher addressed the disciples who delight in his teaching:

verses.pali: มาระเสนา อะภิกกันตา เต วิชานาถะ ภิกขะโว.
verses.english: Māra's army has come on — know them, bhikkhus!

verses.pali: เต จะ อาตัปปะมะกะรุง สุต์วา พุทธัสสะ สาสะนัง
verses.pali_roman: Te ca ātappamakaruṃ sutvā buddhassa sāsanaṃ
verses.english: And they roused their ardour, hearing the Buddha's teaching.

verses.pali: วีตะราเคหิ ปักกามุง เนสัง โลมัมปิ อิญชะยุง.
verses.english: The army withdrew from those free of lust; not a hair of them stirred.

verses.pali: สัพเพ วิชิตะสังคามา ภะยาตีตา ยะสัสสิโน
verses.english: All of them have won the battle, gone beyond fear, and are glorious;

verses.pali: โมทันติ สะหะ ภูเตหิ สาวะกา เต ชะเนสุตาติ.
verses.pali_roman: Modanti saha bhūtehi sāvakā te janesutāti.
verses.english: they rejoice together with the spirits — those disciples of yours, renowned among people.

batch_status.pali_untouched: Typed from MAGNIFIED crops of this sheet — each column in three bands at 2.6×, the colophon and the footnote at 3.2× — and then compared line by line with the roman twin at verses 172-192, which maps onto the 21 rows one for one.
batch_status.page_scan: agrees. One two-column block of twenty-one verses, then the closing, then the source. A full-width ink profile returns 24 bands and every one is accounted for.
batch_status.notes: Page 182 ENDS THE MAHĀSAMAYA SUTTA, and with it the last continuing chant in the book's Pali-only pass. ⚠ THE WHOLE-PAGE GUTTER PROFILE FAILED HERE — the centred colophon spans the corridor, so the sheet reads as one column until the two-column block is profiled on its own (216px at x 920-1135). Same trap as page 170. ⚠ สันนังกุมาโร has double น and อุปปันโน has double ป, against the twin's Sanaṅkumāro and Upapanno; the second pair are different words, not spellings, and is worth putting to the book. The colophon takes a full stop where page 158's did not, and its gender agreement is correct. Nothing normalised.
